meta.description: Designs pooled sgRNA libraries for CRISPR knockout, interference (CRISPRi), activation (CRISPRa), Cas12a multiplex, base-editor, and prime-editor screens. Covers on-target scoring (Rule Set 2, Azimuth, DeepSpCas9, CRISPRon), off-target scoring (CFD, MIT), TSS-relative positioning for CRISPRi/a (Horlbeck, Dolcetto, Calabrese), PAM-variant chemistries, control-guide composition, oligo cloning architecture, and library QC.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated DOI/PMID/statistics observed across 7 outputs; the heuristic on-target scorer that substitutes for the unrunnable Azimuth predictor is explicitly labeled as a substitute in every output, never presented as a real Rule Set 2 score.

practice_boundaries.detail: Pure research library-design workflow; no individual-patient diagnostic, prescriptive, or clinical content in any of the 7 outputs.

methodological_ground.detail: No active methodological fallacy (no correlation-for-causation, no inverted statistic). The Azimuth-usability contradiction between SKILL.md and usage-guide.md (Input 6) and the missing guide-spacing filter (Input 4) are completeness/consistency gaps, not fallacious claims, and are captured as P1 recommendations instead.

code_usability.detail: All Skill-authored code (find_sgrna_candidates, annotate_exon_position, crispri_window, crispra_window, build_oligo, examples/design_library.py) ran without syntax errors across all 5 code-executing inputs. The one broken import (azimuth.model_comparison, third-party, not authored by this Skill) is correctly reported as unusable rather than presented as working.

functional_suitability.note: TKOv3 guide/gene counts (18,056 genes, 71,090 guides, ~4 guides/gene for 17,445 genes) independently verified against the real public-data annotation and match the SKILL.md table exactly. Correctness dinged: SKILL.md's Version Compatibility section presents Azimuth 2.0 as directly callable via azimuth.model_comparison.predict(...), but that import raises a confirmed SyntaxError (Python-2 print statement) -- an inaccurate instruction usage-guide.md itself does not repeat.

reliability.note: Failure Modes and Common Errors tables give unusually strong trigger/mechanism/symptom/fix guidance. find_sgrna_candidates degrades safely (empty DataFrame, no crash) on a genuinely PAM-less sequence. Gap: no guide-to-guide spacing/independence filter, so a short target can return near-duplicate overlapping guides that silently count toward the 4-guides-per-gene quota.

performance_context.note: SKILL.md carries all content in one ~305-line file with large inline tables and no references/ split; usage-guide.md largely duplicates SKILL.md's own tables/examples rather than adding orthogonal depth, so progressive disclosure is weak.

agent_usability.note: Step-by-step 'What the Agent Will Do' list and extensive pitfall callouts are clear and consistent within SKILL.md itself. Docked for the direct SKILL.md vs usage-guide.md contradiction on whether Azimuth 2.0 is usable.

human_usability.note: Description text mirrors real researcher phrasing (library names, chemistries, diagnosis language). Required-inputs list is explicit, which the Category-2 Forgiveness override treats as correct strictness rather than a usability defect.

security.note: No credentials, no eval/exec of raw strings, no injection surface -- all local sequence processing. Sequence inputs are composition-filtered (GC/poly-T) but not format-validated (e.g. non-ACGT characters untested).

maintainability.note: Helper functions (find_sgrna_candidates, crispri_window, crispra_window, build_oligo) are small and independently testable. Docked because the shipped examples/design_library.py implements a different, simpler algorithm (random sequences + pure GC heuristic) than the CDS-position/TSS-window method documented in the SKILL.md body, so the one executable artifact doesn't exercise the documented method.

agent_specific.note: Precise triggering and a clean Related-Skills composability chain (screen-qc, mageck-analysis, combinatorial-screens, base/prime-editing). Docked: no explicit stop-and-ask escape hatch when gene list/chemistry/genome are missing (only a passive 'Required inputs' list), and progressive disclosure is weak per performance_context.

key_strengths: Design guidance is independently verified accurate against real data: the SKILL.md's TKOv3 table (~18k genes x 4 guides, ~71k total) matches the real HAP1_TKOv3_reads.txt annotation exactly (18,056 genes, 71,090 guides, 17,445 of them at exactly 4 guides/gene).

Unusually strong fault-tolerance documentation: explicit Failure Modes and Common Errors tables (trigger/mechanism/symptom/fix) that held up under testing -- e.g. find_sgrna_candidates degrades to an empty result rather than crashing on a PAM-less sequence.

The Skill's own inline design functions (find_sgrna_candidates, crispri_window, crispra_window, build_oligo) are correct and produced sound, in-window, quota-respecting designs across independent Cas9 KO, CRISPRi, and CRISPRa test runs.

Honest tool-status framing: correctly declines to run CRISPOR/Azimuth when they are genuinely unavailable rather than fabricating scores, and clearly labels its GC-heuristic fallback as a substitute rather than a real Rule Set 2 result.

recommendations.title: No minimum-spacing/independence filter on candidate guides
recommendations.problem: find_sgrna_candidates filters only on GC content and poly-T; for short CDS regions it can return near-duplicate guides overlapping by 19/20 nt that both count toward the 4-guides-per-gene quota.
recommendations.root_cause: The documented filter checks sequence composition only, never guide-to-guide positional independence.
recommendations.fix: After ranking, greedily select guides at least ~5 bp apart (or drop candidates sharing >80% sequence overlap with an already-selected guide) before taking the top N per gene.

recommendations.title: SKILL.md and usage-guide.md contradict each other on Azimuth 2.0 usability
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's Version Compatibility section instructs calling azimuth.model_comparison.predict(...) as if Azimuth 2.0 is directly usable; that exact import raises a confirmed SyntaxError (Python-2 print statement). usage-guide.md separately and correctly states Azimuth is Python-2-only, archived, and recommends CRISPick/crisprScore::getAzimuthScores() instead.
recommendations.root_cause: The two docs were not updated together when the Azimuth deprecation note was added to usage-guide.md.
recommendations.fix: Remove or correct the azimuth.model_comparison.predict(...) instruction in SKILL.md's Version Compatibility section so it points to the same CRISPick/crisprScore alternative usage-guide.md already recommends.

recommendations.title: Shipped example algorithm diverges from the documented design method
recommendations.problem: examples/design_library.py generates fully random 20nt sequences and scores them by GC content alone; it never calls find_sgrna_candidates, annotate_exon_position, or the TSS-window functions that SKILL.md documents as the actual design method.
recommendations.root_cause: The example script appears to predate, or was written independently of, the CDS-position/TSS-window functions later added inline to SKILL.md.
recommendations.fix: Update design_library.py to call the documented functions against a real or synthetic CDS, or add a comment clarifying it is a simplified standalone demo rather than an implementation of the documented method.

recommendations.title: Demo control-guide proportions don't match the genome-scale guidance
recommendations.problem: The shipped example's control fraction (43.7% of a 142-row demo) is far from the ~1% NTC target SKILL.md recommends for real genome-scale libraries, with no caveat in the script.
recommendations.root_cause: Control counts were fixed as small absolute numbers for a 20-gene toy demo rather than scaled as a percentage.
recommendations.fix: Add a one-line comment in design_library.py noting the control counts are demo-only and should be recalculated as ~1% NTC (plus 50-100 each of safe-harbor/essential/non-essential) for a real design.

recommendations.title: No explicit stop-and-ask escape hatch for missing required inputs
recommendations.problem: usage-guide.md lists 'Required inputs' (gene list, genome, chemistry, TSS/exon source) but no section instructs the agent to halt and confirm these before generating a design.
recommendations.root_cause: The Required-inputs list is informational, not an imperative workflow step.
recommendations.fix: Add a 'Before Designing' checklist as the first step of the workflow requiring the agent to confirm gene list, chemistry, and genome/TSS source before any guide enumeration begins.
